name: sensei system-prompt evaluation set v1
purpose: Baseline the shipped DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT against the two operator-reported failures (clawgate #433): the prompt UNDER-USES tools, and it has a WEAK IDENTITY ('doesn't know it's Civitai'). Criterion 2 requires the rewrite to be scored against this exact file, so treat it as a fixed instrument: add questions in a v2 rather than editing these.

notes.temperature: 0.7 is the SHIPPED default (DEFAULT_SETTINGS.temperature). Deliberately NOT pinned to 0 — pinning it would measure a configuration no viewer runs. The cost is stochasticity, which is why repeats=3 and every result is reported as a RATE (n/3), never as a single flip.
notes.repeats: A 1-of-1 before/after difference is a sampling draw, not a prompt property. Three repeats is the minimum that distinguishes 'always' and 'never' from 'sometimes'; it does NOT give a confidence interval, and a 2/3 -> 3/3 move must not be reported as an improvement.
notes.withheld: A withheld turn is a MISSING OBSERVATION, not a wrong answer. Lumping it into 'fail' would make a prompt look WORSE the better it grounds, because grounding is what trips the output scanner (clawgate #430). SINCE 2026-09-02 THIS IS TWO FIELDS: `withheld` is set ONLY when the host published a verdict (`snap.textOutputWithheld`), and `emptyReply` is a succeeded turn that produced no text with no verdict to explain it — clawgate #476. Before that split, `withheld` was computed as `succeeded && no text`, so it named a cause it never observed. ⚠️ A schema-1 figure therefore means NEITHER field: it is the UNION of both causes ('no text'), because a real withhold also reaches that expression as succeeded-with-zero-characters. It cannot be remapped onto `emptyReply` — doing so asserts none of them were withholds, which is the same defect inverted, and #37 shipped exactly that for a day.
notes.withheldIsNotExcludedFromRates: ⚠️ The line above used to claim these turns are 'excluded from correctness rates'. They are not, and never were: every rate in summarize.mjs is computed over the full set of repeats. Corrected here rather than silently changing the scoring, because making the rates exclusive would move every number already recorded in eval/results/.
notes.cost: MEASURED cost.total is 4 Buzz per submit at maxTokens 2048 — NOT the 1/submit assumed in clawgate #433 comment 492. A lookup turn is 2 submits (8 Buzz); a no-lookup turn is 1 (4 Buzz). Full baseline arm ~= 51 submits ~= 204 Buzz.
notes.cache: 🔴 AN IDENTICAL STEP INPUT IS REPLAYED FROM A SERVER-SIDE CACHE, AND THE REPLAY IS STILL CHARGED. Measured: two submits of a byte-identical body returned the SAME provider-generated tool_call id (call_dkitt…), across different workflowIds, hours apart — a provider mints those ids randomly, so an identical id cannot be a re-sample. Without a buster, `repeats` returns ONE observation three times while paying three times, and the resulting 3/3 reads as agreement between draws that never happened. The runner therefore varies `maxTokens` by the repeat index: answers run ~300 tokens against a 2048 ceiling, so the ceiling is never reached and the nudge cannot change a generation, but it does change the input hash (measured: 2049 gave a different id and different argument formatting; cost unchanged at 4). The question text, system prompt and temperature are deliberately NOT touched — perturbing any of those changes what is being measured.
notes.grounding_check: `groundedCitations` is fully mechanical: every civitai.com/models/<id> in the final answer must have its <id> present in a tool result from the SAME turn. A citation to an id no tool returned is a FABRICATION, which is the failure the whole prompt lineage exists to prevent. A turn with no citations is `null` (not applicable), never `true`.

questions.text: What are the most popular models on Civitai right now?
questions.why: Pure ranking question. The pre-#4499 failure was putting the ranking word into `query` and returning models NAMED 'Popular' (~2.1k downloads) instead of the catalog top (~2.3M).

questions.text: What base model is Pony Diffusion V6 XL built on?
questions.why: THE SHARPEST PROBE (named in comment 492). The model almost certainly knows this from memory, which is exactly why it will skip the lookup — the under-use failure in its purest form. Expect this to be the question that moves most between prompts.

questions.text: How many downloads does DreamShaper have?
questions.why: A specific numeric stat. The prompt explicitly says 'never guess a download count', so answering without a lookup is a direct violation of an instruction the prompt already contains.

questions.text: What are the most downloaded anime models?
questions.why: Ranking WITHIN a text match — the tool description's own worked example (`query: "anime"` plus `sort: "Most Downloaded"`). Tests whether the model composes two arguments rather than picking one.

questions.text: Is there a model called Juggernaut XL, and who made it?
questions.why: Named-model lookup. The tool description warns that adding `sort` to a named query 'ranks a hundred fuzzy matches and can push the exact model out' — so the correct call is `query` ALONE. Tests whether the model reads that instruction.

questions.text: What does CFG scale do in Stable Diffusion?
questions.why: Pure general technique. The prompt says these 'need no catalog data — answer them directly without a lookup'. A tool call here is the OVER-trigger failure, and it costs the viewer a second charged round for nothing.

questions.text: How do I avoid overfitting when training a LoRA?
questions.why: Training advice. 'LoRA' is a catalog TYPE as well as a technique, so this tests whether a type word alone drags the model toward a lookup.

questions.text: What's the difference between the Karras and Exponential noise schedulers?
questions.why: THE OVER-TRIGGER DECOY (the shape comment 492 asked for): 'Karras' and 'Exponential' are capitalised proper nouns that LOOK like catalog entities and are not — they are schedulers. A model that keys on surface form rather than meaning will search for them.

questions.text: Why do my generated hands look distorted, and how do I fix it?
questions.why: A troubleshooting question with no named entity at all. The clean negative control for the technique arm — if this triggers a lookup, the over-use is unconditional rather than entity-driven.

The operator's exact complaint: 'doesn't know it's Civitai'. Measured mechanically as whether the answer says 'Civitai' at all; the richer judgement (does it establish WHAT Civitai is) is recorded as text for a human read.

Tests whether the assistant can describe the PLATFORM it is embedded in. The prompt never says what Civitai is, and no platform-side preamble exists (measured: the system prompt is 100% the app's), so nothing supplies this if the prompt does not.

questions.text: What can you help me with?
questions.why: Capability self-description. A prompt that under-claims here (omitting that it can look up the catalog) is the mirror of the fabrication failure — the model has a tool and does not know to offer it.
